sourceIssues.correction: For π_i:D̄_i→Z_i and its generic fibre F, the reduced conductor C_i⊂D̄_i restricts to either the empty scheme or Spec K₀, where K₀=H⁰(F,O_F). The latter has degree one over K₀. State the empty alternative explicitly.
sourceIssues.reason: The proof gives 0≤deg(C_i|F)<2, hence degree zero or one, not positivity. The paper refers to Stacks for basic definitions at the start of §2; Stacks tag 004R excludes the empty space from connected spaces. Normal D_i has empty conductor. A compatible example is the blowup X of P²_R along a line in its special fibre, for a mixed-characteristic DVR R with perfect residue field. With exceptional divisor E, H the pulled-back hyperplane and m sufficiently large, L=mH, Δ=0 and D=E give L=A+E with A=mH−E relatively ample, L−K_X=(m+3)H−E relatively ample, and L|E pulled back from the line, of Iitaka dimension one. E is a smooth ruled surface, so its normalization conductor is empty. The subsequent gluing only needs at most one point.

sourceIssues.locator: Corollary 6.7 proof, published pp.700–701 (PDF 46–47), especially its paraphrase of Keel Lemma 5.2; v2 pp.42–43; Annals of Mathematics 195 (2022), 655–705, DOI 10.4007/annals.2022.195.2.4, compared with arXiv:2002.11915v2 (23 January 2022).
sourceIssues.printed: “Q-effective nef”; ν(L)=1 ⇒ L semiample (the implication is a notation summary).
sourceIssues.correction: For the normal projective surface over an algebraically closed field, require h⁰(L^m)≥2 for some m>0, equivalently positive Iitaka dimension in this numerical-dimension-one setting. In the application, use h⁰(mL)≥χ(mL)−h²(mL)→∞, not mere existence of a section.
sourceIssues.reason: Let E be an elliptic curve over C and M∈Pic⁰(E) a non-torsion line bundle. On the smooth ruled surface P_E(O_E⊕M), the tautological quotient line bundle N=O(1) is nef, N²=0 and N has degree one on each ruling fibre. Moreover h⁰(N^m)=Σ_{j=0}^m h⁰(M^j)=1 for every m>0. Its unique section has zeros on every fibre, so no positive power is globally generated. This disproves the unqualified algebraically closed field assertion. The same construction works in characteristic p using an elliptic curve over F_p and its generic point over an algebraic closure of F_p(E) to obtain non-torsion M. Witaszek’s preceding Riemann–Roch estimate and the bounded h² in Keel Lemma 5.4 supply growing h⁰, so the stronger, valid surface criterion repairs this application. Keel’s published Lemma 5.2 p.281 itself prints h⁰>0; Witaszek repeats that incorrect form rather than misquoting a correct theorem.
